BIVAHENG • DLG • Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG Legal Opinion No. 76 s. 2011 NOV 10 2011 MR. FILOMENO ABITONA, JR. Valencia City, Bukidnon Dear Mr. Abitona: This has reference to your letter requesting this Department's action concerning your unpaid honoraria as members of the so-called City Executive Advisory Council of the City of Valencia, Bukidnon. Per your letter, you, Mr. Santiago Dablio, and Engr. Felino delos Reyes, all former local chief executives of the City of Valencia, were appointed as secretary and members, respectively, of the City Executive Advisory Council by Mayor Leandro Jose H. Catarata. Former Governor Carlos O. Fortich was appointed as Chairman of the aforesaid Council. YOU also represented that YOU announced as Of the City Executive Advisory Council as early as 23 September 2007 during Mayor Catarata's first City address and were made to render services the following month (October 2007. However, you were officially appointed to such positions only on 02 January 2008 upon issuance by Mayor Catarata of your appointment papers. According to you, you have continuously rendered services until the end of Mayor Catarata's term on 30 June 2010 without having been given your respective honoraria. YOU further represented that you and your other companions were personally discontented of your appointments because the same lacked legal basis. Hence, in the same month (January 2008), Executive Order No. 10-2008, series of 2008 was issued by Mayor Catarata. It was provided in Section 7 of the said Executive Order that the Chairman of the City Executive Advisory Council shall receive an honoraria amounting to Php20,000.00/month, Secretary atnounting to Php18t000.00/month, and Members amounting to Phpl 6,000.00/month. It was also provided in Section 10 thereof that the Executive Order "xxx shali take effect on 02 October 2007, seven (7) days after the official pronouncement of the City Executive Advisory Council existence during the Mayor's Annual Address, unless revoked or amended. " According to you, the subject Executive order was submitted to the Provincial Governor of Bukidnon for approval. The Office of the Provinciat Governor referred the subject Executive Order to Atty. Alberto R. Lagamon, Provincial Legal Officer. Unfortunately, Atty. Lagamon declared that EO No. 10-2008, series of 2008 issued by Mayor Catarata was not proper for lack of legal basis and was accordingly returned to the tatter. Thereafter, the subject Executive Order was again referred to Atty. Nony M. Yulo, City Legal Officer, for comment and that the latter concurred to the opinion

2- rendered by Atty. Lagamon. However, Atty. Yulo advised that it was never late to solicit the proper legislative action of the Sangguniang Panlungsod. The issue was again referred to the DILG Provincial Director and Regional Director and their opinions were in contrary to the opinions previously rendered by the Provincial and City Legal Officers. Hence, your referral to this Department requesting the Department's legal opinion on the following issues, which we quoted in toto: "7. 2. 3. 4. Are the legal opinions of both the City and Provincial Legal Officers asserting that the Executive Order issued by the City Mayor needs an ordinance or law to make it legal, enforceable and Executory per Sec. 455 to (Ill) of the Local Government of 1991? Is it mandatory for an ordinance or law to be enacted to support an executive order issued by the Mayor? What is the liability of the City Mayor who issued the executive order creating a Council but failed to pay the honoraria and or salaries of the services rendered by the members of the Council as a result of the Legal interpretation of both the City and Provincial Officers? Are the legal opinion of both the City and Provincial Officers binding upon the City Mayor to follow and enforce?" Your query may be simplified/summarized as follows: Is Executive Order No. 10-2008 creating the City Executive Advisory Council and naming Mr. Abitona and two (2) others as members of the said Council valid? 2. Can Mr. Abitona and the two (2) others claim their respective honoraria from the time they assumed their respective positions in the City Executive Advisory Council in October 2007 up to June 2070 (end of Mayor Catarata's term of office)? At the outset, it may be well to note that Executive Order No. 10-2008 series of 2008, entitled: "An Order Creating the City executive Advisory Council, It's (sic) Secretariat, Prescribing their Duties, Functions, and Compensation Package" was issued by Mayor Leandro Jose H. Catarata on 15 January 2008. Sections L 7, 9 and IO of the aforesaid Executive Order provide and we quote: "SECTION 7. Composition of the City Executive Advisory Council. The City Executive Advisory Council shall be composed of the following officials: 7. Carlos O. Fortich Former Governor Province of Bukidnon Chairman

2. Filomeno B. Abitona, Jr. Former Municipal Mayor Valencia, Bukidnon 3. Santiago Dablio Former Municipal Mayor Valencia, Bukidnon 4. Engr. Felino S. delos Reyes Former Municipal Mayor Valencia, Bukidnon Secretary Member Member "SECTION 7. Compensation of the City Executive Advisory Council and the Secretariat. The City Executive Advisory Council shall receive the following honoraria/allowances: a. Chairman b. Secretary c. Members php php Php 20,000.00/month 18,000.00/month 16,000.00/month The Secretariat shall receive a monthly honoraria of 2. Php4,OOO.OO each; The Council and the Secretariat shall be entitled to 3. travel allowances subject to availability of funds, and accounting and auditing regulations. " "SECTION 9. Breakdown of funding, sources of funding, and the manner of expenditure. xxx 2. xxx SOUrces of Funds. xxx Since the operation of the City Executive Advisory Council started on October 2, 2007, six (6) days after the mayor officially announced the existence of the City Advisory Council and its members presented during his Ft Mayor Annual Policy Address to the Sangguniang Panlungsod, Barangay, Officials of the thirty one (31) barangays, head of offices on both local and national operating in the City of Valencia, and others present in the occasion. The honoraria of the three (3) members of the City Executive Advisory Council namely: the secretary and the two members will be taken from the discretionary fund of the mayor since the operation of the council has no appropriation. Since the executive order creating the City Executive Advisory Council was signed by the mayor on January 75, 2008 after the annual budget for the 2008 was already approved and made active, the funding for the operation of the City Executive Advisory Council shall be funded through a supplementary budget. Meantime, the monthly honoraria of the City Executive

Advisory Council members shall be temporarily taken from the mayor's discretionary fund or any other source duly recommended and/or advised by the City Budget Officer refundable upon the approval of the supplemental budget for the purpose. " "SECTION 70. Effectivity Clause. This Order shall take effect on October 2, 2007, seven (7) days after the official pronouncement of the City Executive Advisory Council existence during the Mayor's Annual Policy Address, unless revoked or amended. " While the subject EO was dated 15 January 2008, according to you, you were already announced to the public as members of the said Council, made to assume to your respective positions as early as October 2007, but issued with corresponding appointment papers only on 02 January 2008. Your prior assumption to your respective positions is perhaps the reason why the effectivity of the subject Executive Order was made retroactive on 02 October 2007. You and Messrs. Dablio and delos Reyes have continuously rendered services in the City Executive Advisory Council until the end of Mayor Catarata's term of office on 30 June 2010. In sum therefore, you, Mr. Dabio and Mr. delos Reyes rendered actual services as members of the so-called City Executive Advisory Council from October 2007 up to June 2010 or for almost thirty (30) months. In the intervening time, copies of Executive Order No. 10-2008, series of 2008 were submitted to Governor Jose Mae Zubiri, Jr., Province of Bukidnon, for the latter's exercise Of his Section 30 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 71 60) provides and we quote: "SECTION 30. Review of Executive Orders.—(a) Except as otherwise provided under the Constitution and special statutes, the governor shall review all executive orders promulgated by the component city or municipal mayor within his iurisdiction. The city or municipal shall review all executive orders promulgated by the punong barangay within his jurisdiction. Copies of such orders shall be forwarded to the governor or the city or municipal mayor, as the case may be, within three (3) days from their issuance. In all instances of review, the local chief executive concerned shall ensure that such executive orders are within the powers granted by law and in conformity with provincial, city, or municipal ordinances. (b) If the qovernor or the city or municipal mayor fails to act on said executive orders within thirty (30) days after their submission, the same shall be deemed consistent with law and therefore valid. " (Emphasis Supplied)

5- Per your letter, the Office of the Governor referred EO No. 10-2008, series of 2008 to Atty. Alberto R. Lagamon, Provincial Legal Officer, for the latter's review. Thru a Memorandum for Governor Jose Mae Zubiri, Jr., Province of Bukidnon, dated 20 October 201 1, Atty. Alberto R. Lagamon, Provincial Legal Officer declared that the subject EO is not in proper order for lack of legal basis. Coming now to the first issue raised above, Valencia City is a component city of the Province of Bukidnon. Based on the aforequoted provision of the Local Government Code of 1991, all executive orders promulgated by the component city or municipal mayor shall be forwarded to the governor within three (3) days from their issuance. If the governor fails to act on said executive orders within thirty (3) days after their submission, the same shall be deemed consistent with law and therefore valid. Upon perusal of the copy of Executive Order No. 10-2008 attached to your lette, the same was dated 15 January 2008. May we note that there was no representation by Mr. Abitona as to the exact date the copy of the EO was submitted to the Office of the Governor. Be that as it may, it is a legal presumption, born of wisdom and experience, that official duty has been regularly performed. Applying this legal presumption to the case at hand, the copy of EO No. 10-2008 issued by Mayor Catarata of the City of Valencia should have been submitted to the Office of the Governor days from its issuance. On the other hand, the Memorandum of Atty. Lagamon for Governor Zubiri declaring EO No. 10-2008 to be without legal basis was dated 20 October 2008. We observed that such declaration made by Atty. Lagamon has obviously gone beyond the reglementary period of 30 days under the aforequoted provision of the Local Government Code of 1991. Due to such inaction, we are of the view that the subject EO should be considered consistent with law and therefore valid. We are of the further view that the declaration made by Atty. Lagamon has no longer any effect on the EO as the latter was already rendered consistent with law and valid. Hence, any question assailing the validity of the subject EO should be property threshed out through appropriate action before the proper forum, With regard to the second issue on your claim for honoraria, we are of the view that you are entitled to honoraria from the time you have assumed your respective positions until 30 June 2010, the end of Mayor Catarata's term of office, this being one of the logical consequences of the validity of the EO. Assuming that the legal presumption on performance of official duty on the part of the City of Valencia as discussed above is rebutted (i.e. pieces of evidence were shown that the subject EO was not submitted 3 days from its issuance to the Office of the Governor but way beyond such period), we are of the view that you and your companions are still entitled to honoraria from the time you have assumed your respective positions until 30 June 2010 based on the de facto doctrine in public office. The de facto doctrine refers to the principle which holds that a person who, by the proper authority, is admitted and sworn into office is deemed to be rightfully in such office until, by judicial declaration in a proper proceeding, he is ousted therefrom, or his admission thereto is declared void (63A Am. Jur. 2d 1081 as cited in the Law on Public Officers and Election Law, de Leon and de Leon, Jr., 3rd ed., p. 106). A de facto officer is thus defined by the Supreme Court in the case of Torres vs. Ribo, 81 Phif 44, as one who has the reputation of being the officer that he

assumes to be, and yet is not a good officer in point of law. He must have acted as officer for such length of time, under color of title and under such circumstances of reputation or acquiescence by the public and public authorities, as to afford a presumption of election or appointment, and induce people, without inquiry, and relying on the supposition that he is the officer he assumes to be, to submit to or invoke his action. We hope we have sufficiently addressed your concern. Very truly ATTY. JESUS DOQ EIV Direc or Ill Ls/17 Copy furnished: MAYOR LEANDRO JOSE H. CATARATA Valencia City, Bukidnon GOVERNOR JOSE MA. R.
